messages:
maria (pm): quick proposal — introduce an append-only cryptographic audit layer ("LogSeal") to provide tamper-evident audit records for SOC2/evidence, and a clean migration path for customers moving from hosted -> private with BYOK continuity. key asks: immutability, exportable evidence, and legal-hold compatibility.
ajay (security): love the name 😄 threat model first: where are signing keys kept? customer KMS, Redwood HSM, or hybrid? also need key-rotation proof.
hazel (ops): also need rough perf numbers — signing at ingest adds CPU. what is acceptable p99 write latency bump? storage growth will be non-trivial if we keep both signed entries + indexes.
dave (infra): implementation sketch: sign compact merkle-leaf for each audit event, batch Merkle updates every 10s. verification can be async. ETL for search needs to keep plain-text index separate from sealed blob. example ledger item: ```{"ts":"2025-11-02T12:34:56Z","tenant":"t-123","event":"model.generate","payload_hash":"sha256:...","sig":"base64..."}```
oliver (legal): we need export format that courts/legal teams can consume. canonical JSON + detached signature + signature chain (Merkle root history). also retention + legal hold must allow freeze-without-delete.
nina (sales): customers keep asking for BYOK escrow automation during migrations. If they bring a key to hosted now and later go private, we need a documented handshake so logs remain verifiable. this would be a big sell.
ajay (security): proposal: primary signer = customer KMS when available, fallback signer = Redwood HSM. publish signed statement mapping when fallback used: "customer-kms-unavailable -> Redwood-signed-assertion". include non-repudiation metadata.
hazel (ops): rollout concerns: indexing pipeline needs to be able to query events without decrypting or verifying every signature. plan: store signed blob in cold store and indexed fields in search DB; verification run on-demand or during export.
dave (infra): estimated cost ballpark: +15–25% CPU on ingest, +40% storage overhead for signed blobs and Merkle metadata. search latency unchanged if we avoid verifying at query time.
maria (pm): launch criteria I propose: 1) evidence export format + verifier tool published; 2) BYOK handshake spec + migration test with 2 pilot customers; 3) perf: write p99 increase <= 50ms on typical event; 4) legal hold freeze implemented. agree/disagree?
ajay (security): add: automated key-rotation proof feature. customers need a way to show signatures pre/post rotation are valid.
oliver (legal): add: retention policy docs with explicit exceptions for legal-hold and subpoena workflows. export SLA must be stated.
nina (sales): pricing/packaging question: will this be included in Dedicated/Private only, or premium hosted add-on? many SMBs want immutability but not BYOK.
maria (pm): thinking: base LogSeal included in Dedicated/Private; hosted add-on for customers requesting attested immutability + BYOK escrow. pilot for two enterprise customers (one using BYOK, one without).
hazel (ops): ops runbook: on signer failover, emit an "audit-sign-fallback" alert and create an exportable attest file. also need replay tool to rebuild Merkle history.
dave (infra): dev tasks: signer abstraction, merkle service, storage schema, export tooling, verifier CLI. rough timeline: 8–10 weeks MVP (pilot), 12–16 weeks full rollout if no surprises.
ajay (security): will prepare threat doc + KMS integration checklist.
maria (pm): next steps: 1) decide signer model (customer-first fallback pattern) — vote now. 2) assign pilot customers. 3) schedule design review with infra + ops + legal. vote: +1 for customer-first fallback, -1 for Redwood-first.
(reacts) maria (pm): +1
(reacts) ajay (security): +1
(reacts) dave (infra): +1
(reacts) hazel (ops): +1
(reacts) oliver (legal): +1

incident-bot: deploy scheduled: design-review doc published to Confluence at https://confluence.redwood.ai/logseal-design (auto).
